**Unstable beta.** Until 1.0, any release may change the public Rust API, the
serialized Contract/Compilation/envelope shapes, the canonical bytes, and every
identity computed over them. Pin an exact version. The Contract format is
**not** promoted to a stable v1 by this release.

This release exists to correct a defect in the two versions before it. Both
`0.1.0-beta.1` and `0.1.0-beta.2` compile a declaration graph by walking it as
a tree, so a sub-kilobyte `.did` file with shared type aliases can cost
exponential work under default limits — and no limit refuses it. If you compile
`.did` source you did not write, upgrade rather than pin either earlier
version.

## Installation

A prerelease is never selected by a caret requirement — name it exactly:

```toml
# Full surface (all features on by default)
candid-core = "=0.1.0-beta.3"

# Pure Contract model — no Candid engine, no filesystem capability crate
candid-core = { version = "=0.1.0-beta.3", default-features = false }

# Model plus the lossless host value ABI
candid-core = { version = "=0.1.0-beta.3", default-features = false, features = ["host-value"] }

# Source compilation with no host filesystem (the browser-WASM surface)
candid-core = { version = "=0.1.0-beta.3", default-features = false, features = ["compiler"] }

# Native filesystem access and the candid-core binary
candid-core = { version = "=0.1.0-beta.3", default-features = false, features = ["filesystem-compiler"] }
```

## What changed since 0.1.0-beta.2

- **The type-depth guards no longer re-expand shared subtrees, and they charge
  for the work they do** (issue #125). Both walks that enforce `max_type_depth`
  treated declaration DAGs as trees, re-expanding a shared subtree once per
  incoming edge — O(2^n) node visits — while charging nothing, because they
  observed only cancellation and deadlines and `compile_did` configures
  neither. On the reported reproduction a 781-byte `.did` burned 5.097 s at
  n = 20 and still returned `Ok`. Each walk now builds a recursion map, tracks
  only cycle members per path, and skips expansion states it has already seen;
  the n = 24 fan-out that needed O(2^24) visits now compiles at a pinned 2 796
  work units. Pruning exact duplicate states cannot change what a walk refuses,
  and the depth pins hold unchanged — this is a cost fix, not a behaviour one.
- **`Limits::max_type_preflight_work` and `with_max_type_preflight_work` are
  new public API** (issue #125), defaulting to 10 000 000. Shapes that still
  multiply states now fail closed with `resource_limit_exceeded` naming
  `type_preflight_work` instead of hanging. The counter also bounds memory, at
  about 19 bytes of peak live heap per unit — roughly 190 MB at the default. A
  browser or other constrained host should lower it to what its heap can hold;
  1 000 000 keeps the walks under ~19 MB and still clears every realistic
  contract by three orders of magnitude. The addition is additive: two inherent
  methods, nothing removed, no break reported against `0.1.0-beta.2`, and
  `LIMITS_CONFIG_VERSION` is unchanged.
- **`candid-core compile <path> --envelope` emits a one-document
  `ContractEnvelope`** (issue #152) — the canonical Contract plus its
  field-name table as the `org.candid-core.field-names/v1` extension, so one
  self-describing document feeds the `@candid-core/schema` npm package's
  `schemaFromContract` with no separate provenance sidecar. Extensions live
  outside `contract_id` and `interface_id` by design, so the document keeps the
  identities of its plain-`compile` sibling. The flag is mutually exclusive
  with `--no-source-info`. No library API changed. This flag exists in no
  earlier published version, which is the second reason this release is due:
  the npm package's install-and-generate on-ramp names it.
- The version bump itself follows the recorded protocol: producer metadata is
  the only observable change, and the release-metadata suite asserts that no
  semantic identity and no frozen exact-octet vector moved with it.

## Known limitations (carried)

- ADR verification remains incomplete: ADR 0002 is **Verified**; ADRs 0001 and
  0003–0007 remain **Implemented, verification pending**.
- The HostValue ↔ Candid binary bridge is still deferred; bounded JSON decoding
  remains coarse; `HostValue` still gates on `max_value_bytes` with its own
  error shape; raising `max_value_nesting` above 128 still has no effect
  beneath serde_json's ceiling.
- `max_type_preflight_work` bounds the depth guards' own work. A host whose
  allocator fails before the counter does gets an allocation abort in place of
  the structured refusal, so constrained hosts should set the limit explicitly
  rather than rely on the default.
- The TypeScript schema runtime published as `@candid-core/schema`, and the
  `@candid-core/cli` wasm package prepared alongside it, version independently
  and are not part of this crate's published surface.

## Irreversibility

A published crates.io version can never be deleted or replaced; yanking only
stops new resolution. Because a caret requirement never selects a prerelease,
a broken beta reaches only consumers who pinned it exactly.
